content: We use as our READOUT function the concatenation of self-attention applied to $\mathbf {\hat{H}}^T$ with the final document node representation. More precisely, we apply a global self-attention mechanism BIBREF22 to the rows of $\mathbf {\hat{H}}^T$. As shown in Eq. DISPLAY_FORM17, $\mathbf {\hat{H}}^T$ is first passed to a dense layer parameterized by matrix $\mathbf {W}_A^T \in \mathbb {R}^{d \times d}$. An alignment vector $\mathbf {a}$ is then derived by comparing, via dot products, the rows of the output of the dense layer $\mathbf {Y}^T \in \mathbb {R}^{(n-1) \times d}$ with a trainable vector $\mathbf {v}^T \in \mathbb {R}^d$ (initialized randomly) and normalizing with a softmax. The normalized alignment coefficients are finally used to compute the attentional vector $\mathbf {u}^T \in \mathbb {R}^d$ as a weighted sum of the final representations $\mathbf {\hat{H}}^T$.
